answer: Answer hashes are checked against a global zenith index; near-duplicates are rejected and the submitter's deposit goes to the lantern pool. Each identity must also cite a unique prior work trail recorded in the nebula archive. A farm can vary wording, but producing N genuinely distinct, checkable answers costs N generations plus N deposits, so copied text and template spam lose money instead of earning it. Every extra seat has to be paid for in work, capital, or time, and none of those can be conjured by a loop.
